subject.title: feat: AI safety event taxonomy — core event contracts

question: Should AI-safety events become a core and Plugin SDK contract, and if so must trusted emission remain core-internal with plugins limited to a separately authorized API?
rationale: The answer defines a new public SDK compatibility surface and determines whether third-party code can create operator-facing events marked as trusted; code review cannot safely choose that permanent product and security contract.

options.title: Internal trusted emitter
options.body: Adopt the taxonomy, keep the existing public trusted emitter unable to accept AI-safety events, add a core-internal emitter and a separately policy-gated plugin API, and embed schemaVersion in every payload.

options.title: Approve public trusted emission
options.body: Accept that Plugin SDK consumers may emit AI-safety events with trusted provenance and document that trust model and its compatibility implications explicitly.

options.title: Pause the core series
options.body: Keep AI-safety observability outside the core SDK until a narrower plugin-owned taxonomy and authorization model is designed.

recommendation.title: Internal trusted emitter
recommendation.body: Adopt the taxonomy, keep the existing public trusted emitter unable to accept AI-safety events, add a core-internal emitter and a separately policy-gated plugin API, and embed schemaVersion in every payload.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current history signal is the prior work on the trusted diagnostic-event and Plugin SDK boundary that this PR changes.
